findings.title: delegation-reminder.md tool-registry pointer resolves nowhere
findings.evidence: The rewritten hot-lane payload (cat {HOOKS}/delegation-reminder.md, hooks/hooks.json wiring[5]) replaced the working absolute path 'Tool registry: ~/Repos/.claude/skills/CORE/tools.md' with 'Tool registry: skills/CORE/tools.md.'. That path does not exist in this registry repo (no skills/CORE/), does not exist at ~/Repos/skills/CORE/tools.md, and is not app-repo-relative either — verified on disk. Every prompt in every harness now receives a dead pointer; this file is the canon payload, not a per-harness render, so no placeholder rewrites it.
findings.fix: Restore the resolvable reference in hooks/delegation-reminder.md (and re-run harness-sync --all so consumers pick it up): 'Tool registry: ~/.claude/skills/CORE/tools.md' or the original '~/Repos/.claude/skills/CORE/tools.md'.

findings.title: delegation-reminder.md reformat deletes the standing git-boundary hot-lane guard
findings.evidence: The reformat of the every-prompt payload silently deleted two enforcement-bearing lines, not prose: 'Git (root repo only): changes under ~/Repos outside app repos, commit + push. Never commit across repo boundaries in one operation.' and the deeper-recall channel line ('qmd query ... cass search ...'). The cross-repo-commit rule was the only per-prompt guard against committing across repo boundaries in one operation; nothing in the new text carries it. A rewrite presented as retitling/trim should not drop gate-bearing lines without a replacement.
findings.fix: Re-add the cross-repo git-boundary sentence to hooks/delegation-reminder.md (one line), or record in the bead that the rule moved to an enforcement surface (PreToolUse guard) and cite it.

findings.title: 07/12 bare-checkout SKIP is promised 'disclosed' but is invisible to the runner
findings.evidence: CONSUMER checks 07/12 now return 0 while printing 'SKIP — consumer root ... absent' only to STDERR to make bare checkouts green (lint/checks/07-consumer-symlinks.py:43). run.py builds result 'findings' from stdout lines plus stderr lines that start with 'FAIL' (run.py:151-156); the SKIP line is neither, and the ok path prints nothing to stdout. So --json and the human table both show 'ok' with empty detail on CI: the disclosed skip exists nowhere in the machine-readable record — exactly the empty-is-not-clean blindness check 07's own header warns about ('a skip ... never a false pass on a bare run' is now unverifiable).
findings.fix: In lint/run.py, include stderr lines matching /^(07-consumer-symlinks|12-deployed-app-conformance): SKIP/ (or generalize: any '^\S+: SKIP' line) in the findings array, or have the checks print the SKIP notice to stdout on the green path.
